extra.message: User-controlled `name` parameter (from request.post()['name'] in views.py:57) is interpolated into SQL query using Python's `%` string formatting. This allows arbitrary SQL execution. The README documents exploitation: `Robert'); DROP TABLE students CASCADE; --`.

User-controlled `id_` parameter (from session user_id) is used in SQL query. While parameterized, if user_id is not validated as int, injection is possible. The function does not validate the type of id_.
AIOHTTP application is created with `debug=True`, which exposes stack traces, internal settings, and request details on errors. This is a security misconfiguration suitable only for development.

The `csrf_middleware` defined in sqli/middlewares.py:26-38 is commented out from the middleware list. All POST forms (login, logout, add student, add course, add review, evaluate) are vulnerable to CSRF attacks. Although forms include a `_csrf_token` hidden field, no validation occurs.

Jinja2 is configured with `autoescape=False`, meaning all HTML templates render unescaped content. User-supplied data (review text, course title, course description, student name) is rendered as raw HTML, enabling stored XSS attacks throughout the application.

User-supplied `review.review_text` is rendered without the `| e` escape filter, allowing stored XSS. The README documents this as an exploitable stored XSS vulnerability using `<script>alert(...)</script>` payloads. Because autoescape is disabled globally, this is fully exploitable.
User-supplied `course.title` and `course.description` are rendered without the `| e` escape filter in the course list, enabling stored XSS. Any user can create a course with malicious content.

User-supplied `name` (student name) is rendered without the `| e` escape filter, enabling stored XSS. The student creation endpoint (`/students/` POST) requires no authentication, so any unauthenticated attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript.
User-supplied `course.title` and `course.description` are rendered without the `| e` escape filter on the individual course page (lines 14-15), enabling stored XSS.

The `students` POST endpoint at `/students/` does not require authentication. Any unauthenticated user can create new students. Combined with SQL injection in Student.create, this allows unauthenticated attackers to drop tables and tamper with data.
The `courses` POST endpoint at `/courses/` does not require authentication or admin role. Any unauthenticated user can create new courses, enabling stored XSS injection.
The `review` POST endpoint at `/courses/{course_id}/review` does not require authentication. Any unauthenticated user can post reviews, which then render with stored XSS.

The `evaluate` endpoint has no `@authorize()` decorator and no authentication or admin role check. Any unauthenticated user can submit marks (grades) for any student on any course, allowing attackers to corrupt academic records.

After successful login, the session is not regenerated (no `session.invalidate()` or new session ID). The session ID assigned before authentication remains the same, allowing session fixation attacks. The README documents this as a known vulnerability.

Session cookie is created with `httponly=False`, making it accessible to JavaScript. Combined with stored XSS, attackers can steal session cookies via document.cookie. The cookie is also missing the `secure=True` flag, allowing transmission over HTTP.

extra.message: Passwords are stored and compared using unsalted MD5 hash. MD5 is cryptographically broken, fast, and vulnerable to rainbow table attacks. Use a slow, salted password hash like bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt.

extra.message: Hardcoded weak default credentials in fixtures: `superadmin:superadmin`, `j.doe:password`, `s.king:password`, `p.parker:spidey`. The admin account uses the same string for username and password.

Database credentials (user: 'postgres', password: 'postgres') are hardcoded in config/dev.yaml. While marked as 'dev', the same configuration pattern is used for the application and is committed to the repo.

The 50x error template renders `{{ error.__dict__ }}` in a `<pre>` block, exposing all internal exception attributes to users. Combined with `debug=True`, this leaks stack traces and internal state on any server error.

extra.message: The login endpoint (`index` POST) has no rate limiting, account lockout, or brute-force protection. Combined with weak password hashing and weak default passwords, this allows trivial credential stuffing and password brute-force attacks.

extra.message: Password comparison uses `==` operator on MD5 hashes, which is vulnerable to timing side-channel attacks. Use `hmac.compare_digest()` for constant-time comparison.
